q-46070.name: Question 1
q-46070.problem:
A factory with $150$ machines produces $600\,000$ baseball balls weekly. To determine the number of balls produced by a machine on average, the owner of the factory uses the formula

$$
P=\frac{b}{m},
$$

 
where $b$ is the number of balls produced by the factory weekly, and $m$ is the number of machines in the factory.

What is an appropriate measurement unit for $P?$
q-46070.worked_solution:
We are solving for measurement units, so we can ignore the quantities $150$ and $600\,000.$ They do not matter, if we are just solving for units.

Since $b$ represents $\text{balls}$ and $m$ represents $\text{machines},$ the appropriate measurement unit for $P=\frac{b}{m}$ is $\frac{\text{balls}}{\text{machines}}.$

q-46070.html:
Question 1
?

A factory with 150 machines produces 600000 baseball balls weekly. To determine the number of balls produced by a machine on average, the owner of the factory uses the formula P=bm, where b is the number of balls produced by the factory weekly, and m is the number of machines in the factory.

What is an appropriate measurement unit for P?

a
ballsmachine
b
machinesball
c
machines2ball2
d
machines2ball
e
balls2machine
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are solving for measurement units, so we can ignore the quantities 150 and 600000. They do not matter, if we are just solving for units.

Since b represents balls and m represents machines, the appropriate measurement unit for P=bm is ballsmachines.

q-46095.name: Question 2
q-46095.problem: The acceleration $a$ of a body is related to applied force $F$ and mass $m$ by the equation $a=\frac{F}{m}.$ If $F$ is measured in Newtons $(\frac{\text{kg}\,\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}})$ and $m$ is measured in kilograms, determine an appropriate measurement unit for acceleration.
q-46095.worked_solution:
We can find the unit of acceleration by substituting the given units of force and mass into the formula and simplifying.

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{\text{kg}\,\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}})}{\text{kg}} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\text{kg}}\,\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}\,\cancel{\text{kg}}} \\  & =\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the unit of acceleration is $\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.$

The acceleration a of a body is related to applied force F and mass m by the equation a=Fm. If F is measured in Newtons (kgms2) and m is measured in kilograms, determine an appropriate measurement unit for acceleration.

a
ms2km3
b
ms2
c
mkms2
d
s2m
e
ms
Submit

We can find the unit of acceleration by substituting the given units of force and mass into the formula and simplifying.

a=Fm=(kgms2)kg=kgms2kg=ms2

Thus, the unit of acceleration is ms2.

q-46152.name: Question 3
q-46152.problem: The speed of a car moving with a constant acceleration is given by the formula $v=at,$ where $a$ is the car's acceleration, and $t$ is the time passed. Given that the acceleration is measured in $\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}$, determine the units of speed in terms of meters and seconds.
q-46152.worked_solution:
Acceleration is measured in $\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}$ and time is measured in seconds. We can find the unit of speed by substituting the given units of acceleration and time into the formula and simplifying. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =a\cdot t \\  & =\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \text{s} \\  & =\frac{\text{m}\,\cancel{\text{s}}}{{\text{s}}^{\cancel{2}}} \\  & =\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the unit of speed is $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.$

q-46152.html:
Question 3
?

The speed of a car moving with a constant acceleration is given by the formula v=at, where a is the car's acceleration, and t is the time passed. Given that the acceleration is measured in ms2, determine the units of speed in terms of meters and seconds.

a
sm2
b
ms2
c
sm
d
ms
e
s2m2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Acceleration is measured in ms2 and time is measured in seconds. We can find the unit of speed by substituting the given units of acceleration and time into the formula and simplifying. v=a⋅t=ms2⋅s=mss2=ms

Thus, the unit of speed is ms.
